paragraphs_in_document_order: Thursday 7 January 2027 | P3 | 40 minutes | Year A

Teach the BUILD group of three to four for forty minutes. Pupils sequence three safe events from their own week so far. They can move cards, point, write or direct an exact scribe. Do not require personal disclosure or public answers.

BUILD Weekly - Spring!C40: Sequence events in my own week. Theme: Resilience & Change. Unit, BUILD - Spring!D10: Then & now, how things change. Term assessment, J10: F: ordering tasks.  S: personal timeline produced.

Success: three real events with a known day or time, in a sound order, using first, next and last through words, position or a supported response. Two events are a useful first scaffold, not the completed three-event goal. Week 1 is formative; Week 6 assesses the six-week sequence.

Put one starter card (Support Cards page 1), three mixed practice strips (Source Cards page 2), the day strip and the visible model at each place. Add the usual writing aid, blank card slips, a book and the chosen route card. Cut strips in advance if needed. A pupil can begin by matching the day labels without waiting for a whole-group question.

Keep three supports visible: a word bank, a sentence starter and a worked model. Here Level 2 names the requested scaffold provision, not an award level. Every route keeps all three supports. Offer a scribed mode on every task. Read short labels privately on request; no reading aloud, cold calling or public questioning.

The week begins Monday 4 January 2027. Today is Thursday 7 January. Friday 8 to Sunday 10 are still to come. The model uses fictional Monday, Wednesday and Thursday events. Use real, low-stakes events from the pupil’s week, such as a class task. Keep names, places, photos of people and personal circumstances out of the record. If unsure, keep the gap and check privately.
Thursday 7 January 2027 | P3 | 40 minutes | Year A
2 minutes private settle; 8 minutes ready starter. Keep day strip, word bank, First is __ stem and three-card model on view.
5 minutes model with a short reset; 5 minutes shared day-order work; 5 minutes choose three actual events and days. All responses stay private or optional.
10 minutes own-week record including a brief reset; 3 minutes private check and response to feedback; 2 minutes exit and evidence capture.

“Here is a made-up week. First I drew on Monday. Next I read on Wednesday. Last I walked on Thursday.” Point to each item from left to right. “Use a safe thing you did. You can point. You can ask me to write. You can pass on a personal detail.”

Offer Monday and Thursday cards: “Show the one that came first this week.” Monday is correct. If unsure, lay out the day strip and trace to each day, then rebuild two cards and add Wednesday. Do not ask a public question or remove the visual aids to test memory.

The pupil chooses each event and day, places or directs the order, and gives words or points to a stem. The adult records exact words or the selected labels, reads them back quietly and invites confirmation or a change. Record the actual prompts and choices. Never invent an event or day to complete the record.

Each pupil has their own three-event record in a book, with days/time order, first/next/last and actual help recorded. A photo of the anonymous card order is optional. If personal events remain unknown, keep the model practice separately and leave the own-week outcome unconfirmed.
Thursday 7 January 2027 | P3 | 40 minutes | Year A

Supported: start with two day/event choices, add a third, point or direct a scribe. Independent: choose and order three actual events using all scaffolds. Aspire: keep three events, explain before/after or add a fourth known event. All routes use the word bank, stem and visible model; the route label does not determine a pupil’s support needs.

Cognition: one step and a small choice set. Communication: exact scribing, pointing, usual aid and quiet wait time; plan in any language. SEMH: safe class events, private prompts and a pass option. Sensory/physical: large cards, adult cutting and usual access aid. Meaning uses words, position and borders, never colour alone.

Evidence HUM-BUILD-S1-W01-E1: individual three-event order, actual dates/days if known, words or selection, and actual support. Use Pupil number: ____ for each pupil. Keep one adult reply, one NS and the pupil’s change in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode before R. E follows actual banking. If scribed, retain who selected the content and what the adult supplied, using roles only.

A helper can use a short task list to do jobs in the right order. Offer the pupil’s authentic sequence explanation to the Communication portfolio. Do not infer independent reading, writing or award completion from a supported order.

resources.title: Staff check and support
paragraphs_in_document_order: Thursday 7 January 2027 | P3 | 40 minutes | Year A

The visible model is fictional: Monday 4 January, I drew; Wednesday 6 January, I read; Thursday 7 January, I walked. First/next/last follows that order. Starter cards differ: Monday I played; Wednesday I rested; Thursday I drew. Do not score copying the model as own-week evidence.

Full day order: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday. The displayed week is 4–10 January 2027. Today is Thursday 7. Friday to Sunday are future days. A planned event is not a completed event.

Check an individual order of three actual, safe events across at least two days, or three events whose within-day order is known. Confirm day/time order privately. Look for first/next/last in words, position or the usual supported mode. Record help. Use two cards as a scaffold, then a third. A pupil who only sorts two has made progress but has not yet met the three-event finish.

Day-name order error: trace the visible day strip and rebuild two cards. Then add the middle day. Within-day error: a day label alone cannot decide which event was first; use a known time cue or keep the order uncertain. Future event as past: mark it as a plan and choose a completed event instead. Unknown event: never invent it.

Give short private prompts: “Show first.” “Use the day strip.” “Keep or change?” Let a pupil pass on details. Use safe class work or an anonymous model for practice. Own-week evidence stays unconfirmed if there are no actual events to support it.
Thursday 7 January 2027 | P3 | 40 minutes | Year A

Use the fourth pupil-number field only if a fourth pupil attends. Leave absent pupils blank. No result is pre-filled. Use the individual evidence record for exact words, selected labels, date cues, feedback and response.

Every task has a visible word bank, sentence starter and worked model: arrival, ready starter, day-order practice, own-event choice, book record, review and exit. Supported, Independent and Aspire retain all three. A scribed response is valid; it does not establish independent writing or reading.

Record the pupil’s chosen event/day and order, write their words or selected labels, then read back privately. The pupil confirms or changes the record. Note each actual prompt. If the adult supplies the order, keep it as supported practice and identify what the pupil later does themselves.

Give an actual audience reply and one NS, then retain the pupil’s response in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode before R. E means actual banking only. This week is formative. The owner sets Week 6 as the assessing then-and-now task. [AWARD] / [QUAL] checks remain separate; no unit completion is inferred.
